deloitte-tmt-predictions-2003-011.note: OECD DSTI paper 85: 3 Austria ~17,000 and Mobilkom ~1,500 3G users at Dec 2003, Orange/SFR launch obligation pushed to end-2004, Vodafone UK only a data card in Feb 2004, handset shortages; Irish Times (19 Mar 2004): Hutchison 3G just over 1m customers across Italy, UK and Hong Kong. Well under 'a few million', incumbents delayed: hit. EC Ninth Report not opened (EUR-Lex returned empty bodies); not needed.

deloitte-tmt-predictions-2003-013.note: Ofcom CM 2005 Fig 3.32/3.49: UK SMS revenue GBP 1.4bn to 1.8bn in 2003, SMS per active customer 7.2 to 9.6 a week; MDA via Light Reading: 20.5bn person-to-person texts in 2003, daily volume 52m to 61m. Volumes and revenue rose strongly, but growth was consumer person-to-person, not business, and consumer volume did not tail off: happened in part, partial.

deloitte-tmt-predictions-2003-014.note: Simpay (Wikipedia): operator scheme formed Feb 2003, renamed Jun 2003, closed Jun 2005 without launch; Wikipedia Mobile payment puts first European phone-payment field trials in 2005. The 'slowly' headline held; the named 2003 operator launches (top-up from phone, credit transfer) were not verified by either grader or by my search, so hit is not supported and partial is the floor the evidence supports. Weakest of the confirms.

deloitte-tmt-predictions-2003-016.note: Telecompaper (14 Apr 2003): full UK MMS interoperability only from April 2003; The Register (May 2004): 55% had MMS handsets but 80% never used MMS, T-Mobile UK 4.39m MMS vs 2.98bn SMS in 2003; Ofcom: MMS ~0.1 per customer per month in 2003, 0.2 in 2004, 'remain small'. Interop part held, handset-driven take-up did not: partial.

deloitte-tmt-predictions-2003-017.note: Ofcom CM 2005 Fig 3.63: UK WAP page impressions per customer 7.8 a month (2002), 14.9 (2003), 21.3 (2004), attributed to enhanced GPRS handsets; GPRS devices ~half of subscribers by Sept 2004. Usage revival as stated in 2003 although revenue stayed small: hit.

deloitte-tmt-predictions-2003-018.note: Ofcom CM 2005 s3.2.6: hotspot usage still low, 'even with thousands of hotspots, coverage is still tiny' next to mobile networks, WiFi viewed as a complement rather than a direct competitor; cellular data kept growing (Vodafone AR 2004 data +25%). No dent to GPRS/3G in 2003: hit.

deloitte-tmt-predictions-2003-019.note: OECD DSTI paper 85: EC permitted T-Mobile/mmO2 3G site sharing in the UK (April 2003) and in Germany (July 2003); Spain allowed 3G infrastructure sharing Jan 2004, Finland Apr 2004. Sharing deals and regulatory easing in 2003 as stated: hit.
